LESSON: HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.2: Historical Development of Agriculture

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Historical Development of Agriculture. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why did people start practising agriculture in Africa?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words
2. give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture
3. describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture
4. show respect and fairness when practising Historical Development of Agriculture

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Historical Development of Agriculture helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURE
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words

What this means
In this part you learn to explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Historical Development of Agriculture” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture

What this means
In this part you learn to give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Historical Development of Agriculture.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture

What this means
In this part you learn to describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Show respect and fairness when practising Historical Development of Agriculture

What this means
In this part you learn to show respect and fairness when practising Historical Development of Agriculture. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show respect and fairness when practising Historical Development of Agriculture.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Historical Development of Agriculture” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show respect and fairness when practising Historical Development of Agriculture. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Historical Development of Agriculture is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Historical Development of Agriculture” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Historical Development of Agriculture. (skill: give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture)

Example 4: Connect “Historical Development of Agriculture” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: show respect and fairness when practising Historical Development of Agriculture)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Historical Development of Agriculture to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words.
3. Practise this skill: give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture.
4. Practise this skill: describe one responsible action linked to Historical Development of Agriculture.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Historical Development of Agriculture from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Historical Development of Agriculture: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Historical Development of Agriculture?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why did people start practising agriculture in Africa?
2. How did Agriculture begin in Africa?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Historical Development of Agriculture means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain Historical Development of Agriculture in simple words.
5. Be able to: give Kenyan school/community examples of Historical Development of Agriculture.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
